approachQuestion.prompt:
Mirror-square threshold

Given a nonnegative integer X, return the largest nonnegative integer r with r*r <= X. 0 <= X <= 10^12. Arithmetic uses a signed 64-bit word, so products of candidate values up to 1000000 fit. Examples: X=26 -> 5; X=25 -> 5; X=0 -> 0. Prefer work that grows least with X, then least storage.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Binary-search integer candidates in [0,min(X,1000000)] for the last feasible square, keeping an answer and moving right after a feasible midpoint.
options.feedback: Search an implicit ordered domain rather than materializing its values.

options.text: Build the list of all squares through min(X,1000000), then binary-search it.
options.feedback: This returns the right root but constructs many unneeded values; compute a square only at each probe.

options.text: Return the first midpoint whose square is at least X.
options.feedback: For X=26 that finds 6 rather than the required floor root 5.

details: Binary-search integer candidates in [0,min(X,1000000)] for the last feasible square, keeping an answer and moving right after a feasible midpoint. Search an implicit ordered domain rather than materializing its values.

Feasible integer squares form a prefix of candidates. Save a feasible midpoint and search right for a larger one; an infeasible midpoint removes it and all larger candidates. The X=0 case still includes candidate zero.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the iterative candidate search described above; count fixed-width multiplication and comparisons as constant time. No recursion or square table is used. Treat 10^12 as the stated safe domain bound, not a precomputed answer table. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

options.text: O(1 + log(min(X, 1000000) + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Halve the bounded integer-root interval using fixed-width scalar arithmetic.
details: The implicit domain contains min(X,1000000)+1 candidates. Halving it requires O(1+log(min(X,1000000)+1)) constant-work iterations, including candidate zero. The cap belongs in the range-sensitive bound; no candidate array is stored.

“O(1 + log(min(X, 1000000) + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The inclusive interval contains min(X, 1000000)+1 candidate integers. Each iteration halves it with constant work; scalar bounds and the saved answer use constant memory, including X=0.
“O(X + 1) time, O(X + 1) auxiliary space”: Candidates are implicit integers bounded by min(X,1000000); no X-entry array is initialized or traversed.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: As the candidate range grows, additional midpoint decisions are required; the range-dependent bound records those probes.
